title: Chapter 31
content:
Holding an unlit cigarette between his lips, Jakyeong stared at the error prompt blinking on his laptop screen and chewed out a vicious curse.

Plunging into the pool had completely fried the micro-camera embedded in his horn-rimmed frames. The sensor was dead, and every saved surveillance log had been wiped clean.

"That rig cost a fortune..."

He tossed the useless glasses and laptop onto the desk with a scowl, then walked over to the floor-to-ceiling windows. The torrential downpour had cleared as swiftly as it began, leaving the poolside terrace deserted. The domestic staff had already cleared the deck, sweeping away the cocktail glasses and caviar platters.

Smoking his cigarette down to the filter, the face of Choi Ki-tae's father flashed in his mind. The man was an exact match for the monster branded into his childhood memories. Seeing him living in luxury and thriving in the underworld proved once again that villainy rarely met its rightful karma in this world.

Jakyeong exhaled a thin ribbon of smoke, reached into his pocket, and smoothed out a crumpled card. It was the personal business card Ki-tae had handed him—the one Il-hyun had flicked to the dirt, which Jakyeong had quietly retrieved the next morning. It bore no name, only a single private number.

After a beat of calculation, he brought up his messaging app:

[Hello. This is Jang Yi-an. Are you busy?]

Bracing his palms against the windowsill, he watched the driveway below while waiting for a response. Headlights cut through the gloom as a sleek sedan pulled up to the front gates. A guest at this hour?

From his vantage point, the angle made it impossible to see who stepped out. Driven by curiosity, he slipped out of his suite and headed downstairs.

Rounding the staircase landing, he caught sight of an unfamiliar woman stepping through the foyer. Dressed in a tailored, elegant sheath dress with her hair swept up into an intricate chignon, she possessed a striking, undeniable beauty. Her curves were alluring enough to turn heads on any street in the city.

Park Tae-soo stepped forward, ushering her with quiet deference toward the private wing—specifically, Kang Il-hyun’s master suite.

"What are you looking at so intently?"

Jakyeong jumped slightly, turning to find the senior housekeeper standing right beside him. He masked his surprise instantly.

"Ah... nothing. Just curious, since I haven't seen that lady before..."

"That is Executive Director Kang’s tutor."

"Tutor?"

"He's been taking private Spanish lessons lately."

Ah. Spanish.

Jakyeong was already fluent. Wang Han had always praised his freakish knack for picking up foreign languages faster than seasoned field operatives.

"She is quite beautiful," Jakyeong murmured.

"The Director has always appreciated beautiful things," the housekeeper smiled fondly. "Be it people, art, or fine objects."

Jakyeong offered a thin, polite smile. Who doesn't appreciate beauty? The only difference was that in Jakyeong's world, beauty was directly indexed to monetary value. Whether something was truly beautiful depended entirely on how many zeros were attached to the payout. Most would sneer at him as a shallow mercenary for thinking that way, but he couldn't care less.

"I'll head back up. Have a good night, ma'am."

Excusing himself, he turned back toward the stairs. He had taken only three steps when a burst of bright, melodic laughter echoed from behind Il-hyun’s suite doors.

["I wish someone would comfort me."]

Jakyeong’s brow twitched. Miserable hypocrite.

Halfway up the flight, the phone in his pocket buzzed. Only three people had access to this burner line: Kang Seok-joo, Kang Il-hyun, and Choi Ki-tae.

The caller ID displayed Ki-tae's number.

Jakyeong took the remaining steps two at a time, stepped into his bedroom, and pulled the door shut before answering.

"Jang Yi-an speaking."

[Well, look at that. It really is you.]

Ki-tae’s tone was bright and casual—hardly the demeanor of a man who had buried his younger brother only hours ago.

[To what do I owe the honor? I didn't expect you to reach out first.]

"Just... checking in," Jakyeong said, pitching his voice into a soft, hesitant lilt. "I felt terrible that we didn't get to speak properly at the temple earlier."

[I wasn't expecting a call, but it's a pleasant surprise. Did you call to comfort me?]

The suggestive undertone in the question was unmistakable. What is with these underworld bastards and their obsession with getting comforted today?

Jakyeong’s eyes darted across the darkened room. Getting close to Ki-tae was essential for peeling back the layers of his father's drug syndicate. He lowered his voice, injecting a delicate tremor of secrecy into his tone.

"Actually... I was wondering if your offer from the other night still stands."

[Which offer?]

"The... steep discount you mentioned."

[A discount on gear? Or... something else?]

At the explicit provocation, Jakyeong didn't miss a beat. "I'd prefer to discuss that... in person."

[Hahaha! You're full of surprises today, aren't you?]

"Please keep this strictly between us. If Seok-joo or the household finds out, it would put me in a very difficult position..."

[Understood. Let's set up a private meeting soon.]

Ki-tae hung up without locking in a specific time or location.

Jakyeong lowered the phone, rubbing his temples with a weary sigh. Ki-tae's easy receptiveness was promising, but dealing with that brand of predator was always a delicate wire-walk.

He sat on the edge of the mattress, gazing out the window. The heavy clouds had completely parted, leaving a pale moon suspended in the center of the night sky like a landscape painting.

He lay down, but his mind remained sharp and restless. After tossing and turning for what felt like hours, the faint rumble of an engine broke the silence below—the Spanish tutor was finally departing the estate.

Despite catching barely three hours of fitful sleep, Jakyeong woke at the crack of dawn.

Finding himself restless, he threw on athletic wear and stepped out onto the courtyard lawn. He’d wanted to jog the perimeter mountain trails, but the security detail at the front gate politely barred him, citing strict orders that the guest was never to leave the grounds unaccompanied. The courtyard was massive enough to get a decent run in anyway.

The German Shepherd that had cornered him days ago was out on its morning patrol with a handler. Jakyeong kept a wary eye on the beast, but the hound remained surprisingly docile, trotting along the manicured lawn without so much as a growl.

Returning inside, Jakyeong took a quick shower and changed. Passing over the broken black frames on the dresser, he picked up a pair of round, silver-rimmed wire glasses. They softened his sharp jawline and suited his features far better than the bulky horn-rims.

Heading down to the dining room, he exchanged polite nods with the morning staff. After ten days under this roof, the rhythm of the household had become second nature.

A spread of fresh pastries and a garden salad was already laid out on the table. As the housekeeper poured him a glass of freshly pressed fruit juice, footsteps approached from the foyer. A fresh cup of black coffee was set opposite him.

Unlike Jakyeong, who enjoyed sleeping in, Kang Il-hyun was an early riser—waking before sunrise to train, eating a hearty traditional Korean breakfast, and appearing at the dining table only when Jakyeong wandered down, taking his coffee as an excuse to linger.

[Buenos dias.]

Il-hyun delivered the greeting in fluent, effortless Spanish, pulling out the chair across from Jakyeong and settling in.

Jakyeong met his eyes and offered a formal bow. "Good morning, Director Kang."

The housekeeper set down a glass of water for Il-hyun with an amused smile. "You seem to be enjoying your lessons, sir. Did yesterday's session go well?"

"Very well," Il-hyun replied smoothly. "At least my teacher doesn't ignore me like certain guests in this house."

Knowing full well the barb was directed at him, Jakyeong kept his head down, focusing entirely on his plate.

As he tore into a pastry and took a sip of the fresh juice, Il-hyun leaned his chin on his palm, speaking in a low, melodious Spanish:

[Yi-an. May I spread your thighs tonight and put my cock inside you?]

Jakyeong choked, spitting the juice straight back into his crystal glass.

He glared across the table, his face pulling into a sharp scowl. Il-hyun was watching him with a bright, charmingly innocent smile.

[Looking at me with those ferocious eyes... it's going to be the death of me.]

Jakyeong’s jaw locked tight.

Oblivious to the filth being spoken, the housekeeper clapped her hands in delight. "My goodness! Your fluency has improved so quickly! What did you just say to him, sir?"

"Ask Yi-an yourself," Il-hyun smiled sweetly.

Jakyeong dabbed at his lips with a linen napkin, forcing his voice to remain level. "I'm afraid... I don't understand a word of Spanish."

The moment the lie left his lips, Il-hyun launched into another effortless stream of rapid-fire Spanish—every syllable dripping with crude, filthy obscenity:

[I'd be overjoyed if you took my cock in your mouth... I've never seen anyone quite as exquisite as you... Your ass is so lovely I want to sink my teeth into it.]

Jakyeong’s knuckles turned white around the handle of his silver fork.

I want to kill him. I want to slit his throat right here on the tablecloth. I want to butcher this bastard into pieces.

While Jakyeong’s blood boiled beneath the surface, the housekeeper continued to beam, gushing about how Master Il-hyun had possessed an exceptional gift for foreign languages since childhood.

Given that the man had just used that "gift" to drive a professional assassin to the absolute brink of homicide without breaking a sweat, the talent was undeniably real.

Jakyeong set his fork down with a sharp clatter and stood up. "I'm quite full. If you'll excuse me—"

"Don't run off just yet," Il-hyun said, cutting him off. "Stay a moment. You won't be seeing me for the next few days."

Jakyeong paused, turning back. "Are you... going somewhere?"

"A regional business trip. I'll be gone for about four days."

Lord. I may not believe in God, but thank you.

Jakyeong fought with everything he had to keep a neutral expression, but the instant relief washing over his features was impossible to completely suppress.

Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed into razor-sharp slits. "You look thrilled."

"Not at all..."

"You're practically glowing."

"Truly... I'm not..."

"Look at that smile trying to break out."

"..."

Knowing the man would keep picking at him until he got the reaction he wanted, Jakyeong clamped his mouth shut.

Il-hyun finished the last of his coffee and gestured toward the private wing. "Come to my suite for a moment."

Jakyeong hesitated. With the target flash drive already located in the penthouse, stepping into Il-hyun's personal quarters held zero operational value.

"I have something to give you. Come along."

Without waiting for an answer, Il-hyun strode down the corridor. Resigned, Jakyeong trailed behind.

Entering the master parlor, Il-hyun disappeared straight into the inner bedroom. Jakyeong had intended to wait near the sofa, but Il-hyun called out from within, urging him inside.

With the filthy Spanish phrases still echoing in his head, Jakyeong’s guard was on maximum alert.

"Hurry up. Don't loiter."

Swallowing his reluctance, Jakyeong crossed the threshold.

A sharp metallic slide clicked in the quiet room.

Jakyeong froze mid-stride, his pupils dilating. The icy, unmistakable ring of a gun barrel pressed firmly against his right temple.

His posture locked into absolute stone. Moving only his eyes, he looked sideways at Kang Il-hyun.

The man was holding the sidearm to his head with a faint, playful smirk playing on his lips.

"Wh-What are you doing...?"

Il-hyun lowered the weapon in a fluid motion, reversing his grip to offer the grip to Jakyeong. "A gift."

Jakyeong let out a long, ragged breath, his heart hammering against his ribs. For a split second, he had thought his cover was blown wide open.

"You mentioned you'd never fired a gun before, right?" Il-hyun said smoothly. "It's nothing complicated. Tae-soo will take you down to the range after lunch to show you the basics."

"Why are you giving this to me...?"

"Keep it on you just in case. And ensure you don't sneak out unattended like you did yesterday."

"You really don't need to give me this..."

"It puts my mind at ease," Il-hyun murmured, his tone softening. "If something happens to you while I'm away, it creates unnecessary complications for me."

Jakyeong looked down at the weapon in his palm. It was a compact .22 caliber semi-automatic—factory fresh, completely pristine, with virtually zero recoil, making it ideal for a novice.

Then his gaze caught the polished grip panel.

Neatly engraved into the metal was a single name: An.

A strange, quiet ripple disturbed the surface of Jakyeong's composure. How was he supposed to process a gesture like this?

"Thank you, Director Kang..."

"If you're truly thankful... how about a kiss?"

Jakyeong looked up, bracing for another sarcastic joke—only for Il-hyun’s hand to shoot out, seizing his wrist.

In a single, effortless sweep, Il-hyun disarmed him, tossing the pistol onto the lounge sofa, and dragged Jakyeong backward. Their momentum crashed onto the king-sized mattress, Jakyeong pinned beneath the man's broad frame.

Before he could form a single word of protest, Il-hyun’s mouth crushed down onto his.

Jakyeong wrenched a hand free, bracing his palm hard against Il-hyun’s shoulder. "W-Wait! That wasn't... I didn't come in here for this—"

"Well, I called you in here precisely for this."

Il-hyun’s dark eyes gleamed with wicked amusement. In a swift motion, he yanked Jakyeong’s shirt upward, burying his face against his bare chest.

Caught completely off balance, Jakyeong shoved hard against his shoulders, but the resistance only seemed to fuel the predator above him—Il-hyun's breathing turning rough and heavy as his teeth sank sharply into the sensitive bud of his nipple, wrenching a strangled gasp from Jakyeong's throat.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • .22 Caliber Handguns (.22구경 권총): Small-caliber firearms with minimal recoil, typically chosen for concealed carry, target practice, or given to novices. Il-hyun custom-engraving the name "An" (from Jang Yi-an) emphasizes his twisted, possessive affection toward his guest.
